newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Harradine says not in deal over Telstra.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Harradine says not in deal over Telstra.

text.p: Australian Independent senator Brian Harradine denied on Monday that he was negotiating a deal with the government to secure his backing for the partial privatisation of telecommunications carrier Telstra Corp.
"Can I just say this to you, it is absolutely fanciful to suggest that there are deals going on in respect of the matters that I've raised on Telstra," Harradine told reporters.
In the past, Harradine has said he would like to see funding for forests in his home state of Tasmania emerge from the planned A$8.0 billion sale of one-third of Telstra.

On the weekend, Melbourne's Sunday Age reported that Harradine had also asked the government to scrap abortion funding under the national health insurance scheme, Medicare, and to stop funding for family planning clinics and tax rebates for in-vitro fertilisation.
However, the newspaper did not link these demands with the privatisation of Telstra.
Harradine has also asked the government to consider selling Telstra through the issue of redeemable preference shares, rather than ordinary equity.

Asked on Monday about reports that redeemable preference shares would increase Telstra's debt levels, Harradine said: "Let's get (Communications Minister) Senator Alston's response to my letter and we'll pursue it from there on."

Harradine and fellow Independent senator Mal Colston are crucial to the passing of the Telstra bill as the government needs two extra votes to pass any legislation in the Senate. All other non-government parties are opposed to the bill.
